newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds up at start on U.S., outlook positive.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds up at start on U.S., outlook positive.

text.p: Danish bond prices were up in early trade on Thursday, fuelled by rises on Wall Street, with dealers predicting greater activity in a positive market.
"The strong American market is helping us up, the positive trend should hopefully spark more activity today after yesterday's becalmed situation," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded 0.31 point higher than Wednesday's close at 113.74 with the yield at 5.91 percent while the forthcoming tone-setting seven percent 2007 bond was 0.37 point up at 106.53, yielding 6.12 percent.
The 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed two basis points to 54. The crown traded at 3.8107 per mark at 0740 GMT, firming marginally from 3.8110.
